newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Argos due to explain Xmas upset.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Argos due to explain Xmas upset.

text.p: British catalogue retailer Argos Plc has some explaining to do when it reports annual results next Monday, analysts said.
Investors want to hear why second half sales slipped unexpectedly and whether the deterioration was just a one off, retail analysts said.

In January, Argos, one of the retail industry's top rated firms, issued a surprise profit warning, saying full year earnings were unlikely to exceed 140 million stg after lower than expected second half sales, including the key Christmas shopping season.
"The key thing is what went wrong before Christmas," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at MeesPierson.
One theory is that the retailer might have lost some of its value-for-money image, while rivals -- particularly Woolworths -- were more aggressive on price, said another analyst.

Pre-tax profits are forecast at between 136.5 and 141 million stg, against 124.4 million in the previous financial year. The dividend is expected to rise to about 16 pence from 13.0 pence. The highly cash generative company also paid a special diviend of 42 pence a share last March.

The retailer's shares plummeted after the profit warning, losing 15 percent of their value in a single day. Argos's will later this month leave Britain's FTSE-100 Index of blue chip stocks, because it has dropped down the rankings in terms of market capitalisation.
"The problem was people's expectations were so high that when it (Argos) faltered the stock was hammered," said Victoria Melendez at Morgan Stanley. She is recommending a neutral stance.
The shares did bounce back strongly and still command a sizeable premium rating. Bubb believes they are overvalued and rates them a sell.

Investors want to see if sales have picked up since the end of December. There are perceptions that early January may have been more buoyant, but since then official statistics have suggested a general softening in retail sales.
Analysts said there were also some concerns on costs, which are estimated to have grown signficantly in the second half.
But despite worries caused by Argos's Christmas upset, other analysts said the shares still deserved a premium because of the quality of of management.

The company expects to add seven percent more space this year, and is looking into opening stores in the Netherlands, but the first store is not due to open until 1998. -- Jane Merriman, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
